line-pahacha-16.english: {0:On the sixteenth}{1: step,}{5: I remembered}{3: the sixteen}{2: Mother}{4: Goddesses,}{8: the sixteen}{7: primal}{9: Shaktis}{6: of creation.}

line-pahacha-19.source: ଉଣେଇଶ ପାହାଚରେ ପତିତପାବନ / ମନ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳ ଅତି ଲଭିବାକୁ ଦର୍ଶନ

line-pahacha-19.grammarNote: pāhācare is locative. patitapābana stands as the devotional focus. labhibāku is an infinitive of purpose in -bāku governing darśana.

line-pahacha-13.source: ଚଢ଼ି ତ୍ରୟୋଦଶ ପାହାଚେ କଲି ଜୁହାର / ତୁମ ଅବତାର ରୂପ ନୃସିଂହାବତାର

line-pahacha-8-f.source: ଅଷ୍ଟମେ ଗୁହାରି କଲି କାଟ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଶ / ମାୟାପୀଡ଼ିତ ଭକ୍ତର ଆହେ ଅବିନାଶ

line-pahacha-8-m.source: ଅଷ୍ଟମେ ଗୁହାରି କଲି କାଟ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଶ / ମାୟାପୀଡ଼ିତ ଭକ୍ତର ଆହେ ଅବିନାଶ

spoken-intro-1.source: ಓಂ ತ್ರಿಲೋಕ ಜನನಿ, ಓಂ ಜಗತ್ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಕರ್ತೆ, ಓಂ ತ್ರಿಮೂರ್ತಿ ಮಾತೆ, ಓಂಕಾರ ಸ್ವರೂಪಿಣಿ, ಪಾಹಿಮಾಂ ಪಾಹಿಮಾಂ ಪಾಹಿಮಾಂ
spoken-intro-1.roman: Ōm trilōka janani, ōm jagat sṛṣṭikartē, ōm trimūrti mātē, ōṅkāra svarūpiṇi, pāhimāṃ pāhimāṃ pāhimāṃ
spoken-intro-1.english: {0:Om, }{1,2:Mother of the three worlds, }{3:Om, }{4,5:Creator of the universe, }{6:Om, }{7,8:Mother of the Trimurti, }{9,10:Embodiment of Om, }{11:protect me, }{12:protect me, }{13:protect me!}
spoken-intro-1.grammarNote: Series of Sanskrit vocatives in feminine gender (janani, sṛṣṭikartē, mātē, svarūpiṇi) combined with the standard Sanskrit imperative verb phrase pāhi mām (pāhi: 2sg imperative of pā 'to protect'; mām: 1sg accusative).

verse-4-part-1.source: ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಿಲ್ಲದ ಭಾಗ್ಯವ ಕೊಟ್ಟು ಕಂಕಣ ಕೈಯ ತಿರುವುತ ಬಾರೆ
verse-4-part-1.roman: Saṅkhyeyillada bhāgyava koṭṭu kaṅkaṇa kaiya tiruvuta bāre
verse-4-part-1.grammarNote: Saṅkhyeyillada is a negative adjectival participle (saṅkhye + illa + ada, 'numberless/countless'). Koṭṭu is past verbal participle of kodu ('to give'). Tiruvuta is present participle of tiruvu ('to turn/twist/rotate').

verse-1-part-1.source: ಹೆಜ್ಜೆಯ ಮೇಲೊಂದ್ ಹೆಜ್ಜೆಯನಿಕ್ಕುತ ಗೆಜ್ಜೆಯ ಕಾಲ್ಗಳ ಧ್ವನಿಯ ತೋರುತ
verse-1-part-1.roman: Hejjeya mēlond hejjeyanikkuta gejjeya kālgaḷa dhvaniya tōruta

words.gloss: upon; mēle, governing the preceding genitive
one; ondu, with the following step

verse-1-part-1.grammarNote: Mēlond is sandhi of mēle + ondu ('upon one'). Hejjeyanikkuta is hejjeyannu (accusative) + ikkuta (present continuous participle of ikku, 'to place/put'). Tōruta is present participle of tōru ('to show/reveal/make manifest').

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय
line-01-jai.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-01-jai.grammarNote: Feminine genitive postposition kī agrees with feminine noun jaya in the conventional celebratory formula.

words.gloss: please take; please do (polite precative auxiliary)

line-03-sun-lije-arji.grammarNote: Compound verb suna līje combines main verb stem sun- with polite precative auxiliary lenā (līje); hamārī agrees in feminine singular with arajī.

line-07-daya-karo.source: दया करो दे दो बाबा कृपा की छाया
line-07-daya-karo.roman: Dayā karo de do bābā kṛpā kī chāyā
line-07-daya-karo.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative clauses: dayā karo and compound imperative de do; kī agrees in feminine singular with chāyā.

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.roman: Tukā kahe sevā merī bholī bhāvaḍī
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.grammarNote: Tukā kahe is the standard third-person singular signature formula; merī, bholī, and bhāvaḍī all agree in feminine singular with sevā.

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया
line-10-utho-panduranga.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga prabhāta samaya ā gayā

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-10-utho-panduranga.grammarNote: Uṭho is an imperative second-person plural/honorific; ā gayā is a compound verb (ā- + gayā) expressing completed arrival with masculine subject samaya.

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.source: वैष्णवों का मेला गरुड़ पार आ गया
line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.roman: Vaiṣṇavoṁ kā melā Garuḍa Pāra ā gayā

words.gloss: of Vaishnavas; of devotees of Vishnu

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.grammarNote: Garuḍa Pāra is an unmarked locative goal of motion; melā is masculine singular governing the compound verb ā gayā.

line-12-garuda-par-se.source: गरुड़ पार से महाद्वार देहरी तक
line-12-garuda-par-se.roman: Garuḍa Pāra se mahādvāra deharī taka
line-12-garuda-par-se.english: {2:From }{0:the Garuda }{1:platform }{5:up to }{4:the threshold }{3:of the main gate,}
line-12-garuda-par-se.grammarNote: Ablative se paired with inclusive postposition taka establishes a continuous spatial corridor between two temple landmarks.

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.source: शुक सनकादिक नारद तुम्बर भक्त हैं कोटि
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.roman: Śuka Sanakādika Nārada Tumbara bhakta haiṁ koṭi
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.english: {0:Shuka, }{1:Sanaka and the sages, }{2:Narada, }{3:Tumburu, }{6:and crores }{4:of devotees }{5:are present.}

words.gloss: the enlightened sage son of Vyasa

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.grammarNote: A list of proper nouns acting as plural subject governing the plural auxiliary haiṁ; koṭi functions as a post-nominal numeral quantifier modifying bhakta.

line-15-trishula-damaru.source: त्रिशूल डमरू लेकर आये गिरिजा के पति
line-15-trishula-damaru.roman: Triśūla ḍamarū lekara āye Girijā ke pati

words.gloss: small hourglass drum associated with Śiva

line-15-trishula-damaru.grammarNote: Lekara is a conjunctive participle ('having taken'); āye is plural/honorific masculine agreeing with the subject Girijā ke pati.

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.source: कलियुग का भक्त नामा बना कीर्तनी
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.roman: Kaliyuga kā bhakta Nāmā banā kīrtanī
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.english: {3:Nama, }{2:the devotee }{0,1:of the Kali age, }{4:has become }{5:the lead singer of praise,}

words.gloss: kirtan singer; lead performer of holy song

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.grammarNote: Kaliyuga kā bhakta modifies Nāmā in apposition; banā is a simple past/perfective verb governing predicate noun kīrtanī.

line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.source: पीठ पीछे खड़ी आके बन्दगी ये जनी
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.roman: Pīṭha pīche khaḍī āke bandagī ye Janī
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.english: {2:Standing }{0,1:right behind his back, }{5:this }{6:Jani }{3:has come }{4:in humble homage.}
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.grammarNote: Pīṭha pīche is a locative phrase; khaḍī is feminine singular agreeing with Janī; āke is a conjunctive participle.

line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.source: उठो उठो श्री साईंनाथ गुरु चरण कमल दिखलाओ
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.roman: Uṭho uṭho Śrī Sāīnātha guru caraṇa kamala dikhalāo
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative uṭho uṭho shows heightened urgency; caraṇa kamala is a karmadhāraya compound functioning as direct object of causative imperative dikhalāo.

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.source: फिर भी अज्ञान सी छाई है तुम्हरी योग माया
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.roman: Phira bhī ajñāna sī chāī hai tumharī yoga māyā
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.grammarNote: Compound phrase 'yoga māyā' acts as the feminine singular subject agreeing with 'chāī hai'; 'ajñāna sī' is an adjectival modifier of state.

line-24-bho-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative structure: 'Bho' introduces the titles; 'bhavatimiranāśaka' is a Sanskrit tatpuruṣa compound (bhava + timira + nāśaka) modifying 'ravi'.

line-32-uthakar-netra.source: उठाकर नेत्र पलकें दीन बन्धु रमाकान्ता
line-32-uthakar-netra.roman: Uṭhākara netra palakeṁ dīna bandhu Ramākāntā
line-32-uthakar-netra.english: {0:Lifting }{2:the eyelids }{1:of Your eyes, }{4:O friend }{3:of the humble, }{5:O beloved of Lakshmi,}

words.gloss: beloved of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī, as fortune and splendour; Lord Viṣṇu

line-32-uthakar-netra.grammarNote: 'uṭhākara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on 'dekho' in line 33; 'dīna bandhu' and 'Ramākāntā' are vocative epithets.

line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.source: सुनाओ मधुर वाणी हरो ताप साईंनाथा
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.roman: Sunāo madhura vāṇī haro tāpa Sāīnāthā
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative verbs 'sunāo' and 'haro' addressed to the vocative 'Sāīnāthā'.

line-36-sahan-karke-aao.source: सहन करके आओ चाहे भेट कृष्ण देवा
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.roman: Sahana karake āo cāhe bheṭa Kṛṣṇa devā
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.english: {0,1:bearing it patiently, }{2:come forth; }{3:one longs for }{4:a meeting, }{6:O Lord }{5:Krishna!}
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.grammarNote: 'sahana karake' is a conjunctive participle modifying 'āo'; 'cāhe bheṭa' has an inverted word order with implied subject ('the world/devotee desires a meeting').

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग अब तो दर्शन दो सबको
line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga aba to darśana do sabako

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.grammarNote: Coordinate imperatives 'uṭho' and 'do'; 'Pāṇḍuraṅga' is vocative; 'to' adds emphatic pleading.

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.source: राई रखुमाबाई मन में आने दो दया
line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.roman: Rāī Rakhumābaī mana meṁ āne do dayā

words.gloss: Rakhumābāī, Rukmiṇī the gold-adorned goddess; consort of Viṭṭhala

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.grammarNote: Vocative direct address 'Rāī Rakhumābaī' governing permissive verbal construction 'āne do' with direct object 'dayā'.

words.gloss: Hanumān, the one with prominent jaws; Rāma’s divine attendant and devotee

line-45-garuda-hanumanta-thade.grammarNote: Plural subject 'Garuḍa Hanumanta' takes the stative participle 'ṭhāḍe' and imperfective verb 'johate'; 'bāṭa' is the accusative complement of the idiom.

line-48-vishnudasa-nama-khada.grammarNote: Appositive proper noun 'Viṣṇudāsa Nāmā' is the subject of the predicate adjective 'khaḍā' with conjunctive participle phrase 'lekara kākaḍā'.

line-49-lekar-pancharati.source: लेकर पञ्चारती करूँ बाबा की आरती
line-49-lekar-pancharati.roman: Lekara pañcāratī karūṁ bābā kī āratī
line-49-lekar-pancharati.english: {0:Holding }{1:the five-flame lamp, }{2:I offer }{5:worship with lights }{3,4:to Baba.}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-49-lekar-pancharati.grammarNote: First person singular verb 'karūṁ' taking 'āratī' as direct object; 'pañcāratī' is governed by 'lekara'.

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.source: उठो उठो हे बान्धव मनाओ ये रमाधव
line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.roman: Uṭho uṭho he bāndhava manāo ye Ramādhava

words.gloss: Ramādhava, husband of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī who embodies fortune and splendour; Viṣṇu

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative 'uṭho uṭho' for devotional emphasis; vocative 'he bāndhava'; second-person plural imperative 'manāo'.

line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.source: कृष्णनाथा दत्त साई पदों में चित्त जड़े साई
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.roman: Kṛṣṇanāthā Datta Sāī padoṁ meṁ citta jaḍe Sāī
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.english: {0:Krishnanatha }{6:fixes }{5:his consciousness }{3,4:at the feet }{1,2:of Datta Sai, }{7:O Sai.}
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.grammarNote: Subject 'Kṛṣṇanāthā' with transitive verb 'jaḍe' (3rd person singular present in poetic Hindi); 'Sāī' is repeated at the end for rhythmic emphasis.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-53-kakada-arati-karata.grammarNote: Participle 'karatā' used as finite present verb with implicit first-person subject; 'Sāīnātha devā' is in the vocative case.

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.source: साईंनाथ के भक्ति ताप से उसको जलाया
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.roman: Sāīnātha ke bhakti tāpa se usako jalāyā
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.grammarNote: Causative/transitive past verb 'jalāyā' taking pronoun 'usako' as direct object; 'bhakti tāpa se' is the instrumental cause.

line-61-aise-datta-deva.source: ऐसे दत्त देव शिरडी रहकर भी मिलते
line-61-aise-datta-deva.roman: Aise Datta deva Śiraḍī rahakar bhī milate
line-61-aise-datta-deva.english: {0:In such a way} {1,2:Lord Datta} {6:meets seekers,} {4,5:even while dwelling} {3:in Shirdi.}

words.gloss: Shirdi (the sacred village of Sai Baba)

line-61-aise-datta-deva.grammarNote: Aise functions adverbially modifying milate. Rahakar is a conjunctive participle (rah- + kar) expressing simultaneous or attendant circumstance.

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.source: सगुण दर्शन पाने जन जन शिरडी आ रहा
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.roman: Saguṇa darśana pāne jana jana Śiraḍī ā rahā
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.english: {2:To obtain} {1:the sacred vision} {0:of your embodied form,} {3,4:multitudes of people} {6,7:are coming} {5:to Shirdi.}

words.gloss: with manifest attributes; embodied divine form

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.grammarNote: Pāne is the oblique infinitive of purpose. Jana jana is a distributive reduplication functioning as a singular collective subject with masculine singular agreement in ā rahā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
I wave in offering; I circle

line-72-arati-utaru-mere.grammarNote: Paṇḍharīnāthā is in the vocative case (Paṇḍharīnātha + ā extension common in devotional Marathi/Hindi verse).

line-73-mere-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative phrase standing in direct apposition to Paṇḍharīnāthā in line 72.

line-80-inta-para-khada.source: ईंट पर खड़ा हुआ है सुन्दर बाबा
line-80-inta-para-khada.roman: Ī̃ṭa para khaḍā huā hai sundara bābā

words.gloss: brick (the sacred brick thrown by Pundalik)

line-80-inta-para-khada.grammarNote: Ī̃ṭa para is a locative postpositional phrase. Khaḍā huā hai is a stative periphrastic construction agreeing with the masculine subject sundara bābā.

line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.source: उठकर भोर में बाबा खड़े हैं ईंट पे
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.roman: Uṭhakara bhora meṁ bābā khaḍe haiṁ ī̃ṭa pe
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'uṭhakara' preceding the main predicate 'khaḍe haiṁ'. Honorific plural verb 'haiṁ' and participle 'khaḍe' with singular subject 'bābā'. Postposition 'pe' is a colloquial variant of 'par'.

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.source: केशवराज ईंट पे खड़े नामा चरण पूजते
line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.roman: Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe Nāmā caraṇa pūjate

words.gloss: King Keśava, the fine-haired lord, here Viṭṭhala

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.grammarNote: Two balanced clauses combined in one line: 'Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe [haiṁ]' and 'Nāmā caraṇa pūjate [haiṁ]'. 'Nāmā' refers to the Marathi saint-poet Namdev.

line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.source: साईंनाथ गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.roman: Sāīnātha guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Sainath, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: Vocative titles 'Sāīnātha', 'guru merī māī', and 'Sāī'. 'De do' is a compound verb (stem 'de' + vector verb 'do') forming a polite/pleading imperative. 'Caraṇoṁ' is the oblique plural of 'caraṇa'.

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.source: दत्तराज गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.roman: Dattarāja guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Dattaraja, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}

words.gloss: King Datta, the given one; Lord Dattātreya

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: 'Dattarāja' is a tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya title (Datta + rāja). Syntax and verbal morphology identical to line 93.

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.source: गई छोड़ कर भव से रजनी तम ने विलय पाया
line-20-gai-chhod-kar.roman: Gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī tama ne vilaya pāyā

words.gloss: having done (choḍa kara = having left behind)

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.grammarNote: First clause gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī uses inverted word order with feminine singular subject rajanī; second clause tama ne vilaya pāyā is an ergative transitive construction where tama acts as subject of pāyā.

line-22-shakti-nahi.source: शक्ति नहीं यत्किञ्चित उसको ना सरका पाया
line-22-shakti-nahi.roman: Śakti nahīṁ yatkiñcita usako nā sarakā pāyā

words.gloss: in the least; even a little

line-22-shakti-nahi.grammarNote: Subject is elided; 'yatkiñcita' is a Sanskrit adverbial loanword ('the slightest bit'); 'sarakā pāyā' is a potential compound verb construction with negative marker 'nā'.

line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.source: तुम्ही हटा कर मुख दिखलाना जन तारो राया
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.roman: Tumhī haṭā kara mukha dikhalānā jana tāro rāyā
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.english: {0:You alone, }{1,2:having removed it, }{4:reveal Your }{3:face; }{6:deliver }{5:the devotees, }{7:O King!}
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.grammarNote: 'haṭā kara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on polite imperative 'dikhalānā'; 'rāyā' is a Marathi-derived vocative honorific ('O Sovereign/Lord').

line-27-sakripa-hokar.source: सकृप होकर अपनी महिमा खुद ही सुनवाओ
line-27-sakripa-hokar.roman: Sakṛpa hokara apanī mahimā khuda hī sunavāo
line-27-sakripa-hokar.grammarNote: 'sunavāo' is a second-person plural/polite causative imperative of 'sunnā' (to hear); 'sakṛpa hokara' functions as a participial adjunct.

line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.source: देखो ऐसे देखे जैसे बालक को माता
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.roman: Dekho aise dekhe jaise bālaka ko mātā
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.english: {0:look }{1:in such a way }{3:as }{6:a mother }{2:looks }{4,5:upon her child!}
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.grammarNote: 'dekho' is a direct imperative; 'aise... jaise' introduces a correlative comparative clause with the verb 'dekhe' agreeing with singular subject 'mātā'.

line-35-hum-hi-apni.source: हम ही अपनी खातिर तुमको कष्ट देते देवा
line-35-hum-hi-apni.roman: Hama hī apanī khātira tumako kaṣṭa dete devā
line-35-hum-hi-apni.grammarNote: 'devā' is a Marathi-influenced vocative form; 'kaṣṭa dete' has an elided auxiliary 'haiṁ' typical of verse.

line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.source: त्वद्वचनामृत प्राशन कर के देहभान खो रहा
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.roman: Tvadvacanāmṛta prāśana kara ke dehabhāna kho rahā
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.grammarNote: Tvadvacanāmṛta is a compound noun: tvad- (your) + vacana (speech) + amṛta (nectar). Prāśana kara ke is an adverbial conjunctive participial clause.

line-89-dvara-pe-baje.source: द्वार पे बाजे बजते ढोल ढमाढम गरजते
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.roman: Dvāra pe bāje bajate ḍhola ḍhamāḍhama garajate
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.grammarNote: Parallel imperfective participles 'bajate' and 'garajate' functioning as finite present tense verbs with omitted auxiliary 'haiṁ'. 'Ḍhamāḍhama' is an onomatopoeic adverb.

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय
line-01-jai.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-01-jai.grammarNote: Feminine genitive postposition kī agrees with feminine noun jaya in the conventional celebratory formula.

words.gloss: please take; please do (polite precative auxiliary)

line-03-sun-lije-arji.grammarNote: Compound verb suna līje combines main verb stem sun- with polite precative auxiliary lenā (līje); hamārī agrees in feminine singular with arajī.

line-07-daya-karo.source: दया करो दे दो बाबा कृपा की छाया
line-07-daya-karo.roman: Dayā karo de do bābā kṛpā kī chāyā
line-07-daya-karo.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative clauses: dayā karo and compound imperative de do; kī agrees in feminine singular with chāyā.

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.roman: Tukā kahe sevā merī bholī bhāvaḍī
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.grammarNote: Tukā kahe is the standard third-person singular signature formula; merī, bholī, and bhāvaḍī all agree in feminine singular with sevā.

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया
line-10-utho-panduranga.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga prabhāta samaya ā gayā

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-10-utho-panduranga.grammarNote: Uṭho is an imperative second-person plural/honorific; ā gayā is a compound verb (ā- + gayā) expressing completed arrival with masculine subject samaya.

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.source: वैष्णवों का मेला गरुड़ पार आ गया
line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.roman: Vaiṣṇavoṁ kā melā Garuḍa Pāra ā gayā

words.gloss: of Vaiṣṇavas; of devotees of Vishnu

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.grammarNote: Garuḍa Pāra is an unmarked locative goal of motion; melā is masculine singular governing the compound verb ā gayā.

line-12-garuda-par-se.source: गरुड़ पार से महाद्वार देहरी तक
line-12-garuda-par-se.roman: Garuḍa Pāra se mahādvāra deharī taka
line-12-garuda-par-se.english: {2:From }{0:the Garuḍa }{1:platform }{5:up to }{4:the threshold }{3:of the main gate,}
line-12-garuda-par-se.grammarNote: Ablative se paired with inclusive postposition taka establishes a continuous spatial corridor between two temple landmarks.

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.source: शुक सनकादिक नारद तुम्बर भक्त हैं कोटि
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.roman: Śuka Sanakādika Nārada Tumbara bhakta haiṁ koṭi
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.english: {0:Śuka, }{1:Sanaka and the sages, }{2:Nārada, }{3:Tumburu, }{6:and crores }{4:of devotees }{5:are present.}

words.gloss: the enlightened sage son of Vyasa

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.grammarNote: A list of proper nouns acting as plural subject governing the plural auxiliary haiṁ; koṭi functions as a post-nominal numeral quantifier modifying bhakta.

line-15-trishula-damaru.source: त्रिशूल डमरू लेकर आये गिरिजा के पति
line-15-trishula-damaru.roman: Triśūla ḍamarū lekara āye Girijā ke pati

words.gloss: small hourglass drum associated with Śiva

line-15-trishula-damaru.grammarNote: Lekara is a conjunctive participle ('having taken'); āye is plural/honorific masculine agreeing with the subject Girijā ke pati.

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.source: कलियुग का भक्त नामा बना कीर्तनी
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.roman: Kaliyuga kā bhakta Nāmā banā kīrtanī
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.english: {3:Nāmā, }{2:the devotee }{0,1:of the Kali age, }{4:has become }{5:the lead singer of praise,}

words.gloss: kirtan singer; lead performer of holy song

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.grammarNote: Kaliyuga kā bhakta modifies Nāmā in apposition; banā is a simple past/perfective verb governing predicate noun kīrtanī.

line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.source: पीठ पीछे खड़ी आके बन्दगी ये जनी
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.roman: Pīṭha pīche khaḍī āke bandagī ye Janī
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.english: {2:Standing }{0,1:right behind his back, }{5:this }{6:Janī }{3:has come }{4:in humble homage.}
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.grammarNote: Pīṭha pīche is a locative phrase; khaḍī is feminine singular agreeing with Janī; āke is a conjunctive participle.

line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.source: उठो उठो श्री साईंनाथ गुरु चरण कमल दिखलाओ
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.roman: Uṭho uṭho Śrī Sāīnātha guru caraṇa kamala dikhalāo
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative uṭho uṭho shows heightened urgency; caraṇa kamala is a karmadhāraya compound functioning as direct object of causative imperative dikhalāo.

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.source: फिर भी अज्ञान सी छाई है तुम्हरी योग माया
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.roman: Phira bhī ajñāna sī chāī hai tumharī yoga māyā

words.gloss: divine power; with māyā, the divine power of concealment

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.grammarNote: Compound phrase 'yoga māyā' acts as the feminine singular subject agreeing with 'chāī hai'; 'ajñāna sī' is an adjectival modifier of state.

line-24-bho-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative structure: 'Bho' introduces the titles; 'bhavatimiranāśaka' is a Sanskrit tatpuruṣa compound (bhava + timira + nāśaka) modifying 'ravi'.

line-32-uthakar-netra.source: उठाकर नेत्र पलकें दीन बन्धु रमाकान्ता
line-32-uthakar-netra.roman: Uṭhākara netra palakeṁ dīna bandhu Ramākāntā
line-32-uthakar-netra.english: {0:Lift }{1,2:Your eyelids, }{4:O friend }{3:of the humble, }{5:O beloved of Lakṣmī,}

words.gloss: beloved of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī, as fortune and splendour; Lord Viṣṇu

line-32-uthakar-netra.grammarNote: 'uṭhākara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on 'dekho' in line 33; 'dīna bandhu' and 'Ramākāntā' are vocative epithets.

line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.source: सुनाओ मधुर वाणी हरो ताप साईंनाथा
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.roman: Sunāo madhura vāṇī haro tāpa Sāīnāthā
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative verbs 'sunāo' and 'haro' addressed to the vocative 'Sāīnāthā'.

line-36-sahan-karke-aao.source: सहन करके आओ चाहे भेट कृष्ण देवा
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.roman: Sahana karake āo cāhe bheṭa Kṛṣṇa devā
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.english: {0,1:bear with us }and {2:come forth; }{3:we long }{4:to meet You, }{6:O Lord }{5:Kṛṣṇa!}
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.grammarNote: 'sahana karake' is a conjunctive participle modifying 'āo'; 'cāhe bheṭa' has an inverted word order with implied subject ('the world/devotee desires a meeting').

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग अब तो दर्शन दो सबको
line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga aba to darśana do sabako

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.grammarNote: Coordinate imperatives 'uṭho' and 'do'; 'Pāṇḍuraṅga' is vocative; 'to' adds emphatic pleading.

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.source: राई रखुमाबाई मन में आने दो दया
line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.roman: Rāī Rakhumābaī mana meṁ āne do dayā

words.gloss: Rakhumābāī, Rukmiṇī the gold-adorned goddess; consort of Viṭṭhala

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.grammarNote: Vocative direct address 'Rāī Rakhumābaī' governing permissive verbal construction 'āne do' with direct object 'dayā'.

words.gloss: Hanumān, the one with prominent jaws; Rāma’s divine attendant and devotee

line-45-garuda-hanumanta-thade.grammarNote: Plural subject 'Garuḍa Hanumanta' takes the stative participle 'ṭhāḍe' and imperfective verb 'johate'; 'bāṭa' is the accusative complement of the idiom.

line-48-vishnudasa-nama-khada.grammarNote: Appositive proper noun 'Viṣṇudāsa Nāmā' is the subject of the predicate adjective 'khaḍā' with conjunctive participle phrase 'lekara kākaḍā'.

line-49-lekar-pancharati.source: लेकर पञ्चारती करूँ बाबा की आरती
line-49-lekar-pancharati.roman: Lekara pañcāratī karūṁ bābā kī āratī
line-49-lekar-pancharati.english: {0:Holding }{1:the five-flame lamp, }{2:I offer }{5:worship with lights }{3,4:to Bābā.}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-49-lekar-pancharati.grammarNote: First person singular verb 'karūṁ' taking 'āratī' as direct object; 'pañcāratī' is governed by 'lekara'.

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.source: उठो उठो हे बान्धव मनाओ ये रमाधव
line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.roman: Uṭho uṭho he bāndhava manāo ye Ramādhava

words.gloss: Ramādhava, husband of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī who embodies fortune and splendour; Viṣṇu

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative 'uṭho uṭho' for devotional emphasis; vocative 'he bāndhava'; second-person plural imperative 'manāo'.

line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.source: कृष्णनाथा दत्त साई पदों में चित्त जड़े साई
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.roman: Kṛṣṇanāthā Datta Sāī padoṁ meṁ citta jaḍe Sāī
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.english: {0:Kṛṣṇanātha }{6:fixes }{5:his consciousness }{3,4:at the feet }{1,2:of Datta Sāī, }{7:O Sāī.}
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.grammarNote: Subject 'Kṛṣṇanāthā' with transitive verb 'jaḍe' (3rd person singular present in poetic Hindi); 'Sāī' is repeated at the end for rhythmic emphasis.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-53-kakada-arati-karata.grammarNote: Participle 'karatā' used as finite present verb with implicit first-person subject; 'Sāīnātha devā' is in the vocative case.

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.source: साईंनाथ के भक्ति ताप से उसको जलाया
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.roman: Sāīnātha ke bhakti tāpa se usako jalāyā
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.grammarNote: Causative/transitive past verb 'jalāyā' taking pronoun 'usako' as direct object; 'bhakti tāpa se' is the instrumental cause.

line-61-aise-datta-deva.source: ऐसे दत्त देव शिरडी रहकर भी मिलते
line-61-aise-datta-deva.roman: Aise Datta deva Śiraḍī rahakar bhī milate
line-61-aise-datta-deva.english: {0:In such a way} {1,2:Lord Datta} {6:meets seekers,} {4,5:even while dwelling} {3:in Śiraḍī.}

words.gloss: Śiraḍī (the sacred village of Sāī Bābā)

line-61-aise-datta-deva.grammarNote: Aise functions adverbially modifying milate. Rahakar is a conjunctive participle (rah- + kar) expressing simultaneous or attendant circumstance.

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.source: सगुण दर्शन पाने जन जन शिरडी आ रहा
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.roman: Saguṇa darśana pāne jana jana Śiraḍī ā rahā
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.english: {2:To obtain} {1:the sacred vision} {0:of your embodied form,} {3,4:multitudes of people} {6,7:are coming} {5:to Śiraḍī.}

words.gloss: with manifest attributes; embodied divine form
the town where Sāī Bābā lived and taught, a destination for his devotees

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.grammarNote: Pāne is the oblique infinitive of purpose. Jana jana is a distributive reduplication functioning as a singular collective subject with masculine singular agreement in ā rahā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
I wave in offering; I circle

line-72-arati-utaru-mere.grammarNote: Paṇḍharīnāthā is in the vocative case (Paṇḍharīnātha + ā extension common in devotional Marathi/Hindi verse).

line-73-mere-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative phrase standing in direct apposition to Paṇḍharīnāthā in line 72.

line-80-inta-para-khada.source: ईंट पर खड़ा हुआ है सुन्दर बाबा
line-80-inta-para-khada.roman: Ī̃ṭa para khaḍā huā hai sundara bābā

words.gloss: brick (the sacred brick thrown by Pundalik)

line-80-inta-para-khada.grammarNote: Ī̃ṭa para is a locative postpositional phrase. Khaḍā huā hai is a stative periphrastic construction agreeing with the masculine subject sundara bābā.

line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.source: उठकर भोर में बाबा खड़े हैं ईंट पे
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.roman: Uṭhakara bhora meṁ bābā khaḍe haiṁ ī̃ṭa pe
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'uṭhakara' preceding the main predicate 'khaḍe haiṁ'. Honorific plural verb 'haiṁ' and participle 'khaḍe' with singular subject 'bābā'. Postposition 'pe' is a colloquial variant of 'par'.

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.source: केशवराज ईंट पे खड़े नामा चरण पूजते
line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.roman: Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe Nāmā caraṇa pūjate

words.gloss: King Keśava, the fine-haired lord, here Viṭṭhala

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.grammarNote: Two balanced clauses combined in one line: 'Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe [haiṁ]' and 'Nāmā caraṇa pūjate [haiṁ]'. 'Nāmā' refers to the Marathi saint-poet Namdev.

line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.source: साईंनाथ गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.roman: Sāīnātha guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Sāīnātha, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sāī.}
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: Vocative titles 'Sāīnātha', 'guru merī māī', and 'Sāī'. 'De do' is a compound verb (stem 'de' + vector verb 'do') forming a polite/pleading imperative. 'Caraṇoṁ' is the oblique plural of 'caraṇa'.

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.source: दत्तराज गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.roman: Dattarāja guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Dattarāja, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sāī.}

words.gloss: King Datta, the given one; Lord Dattātreya

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: 'Dattarāja' is a tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya title (Datta + rāja). Syntax and verbal morphology identical to line 93.

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.source: गई छोड़ कर भव से रजनी तम ने विलय पाया
line-20-gai-chhod-kar.roman: Gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī tama ne vilaya pāyā

words.gloss: having done (choḍa kara = having left behind)

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.grammarNote: First clause gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī uses inverted word order with feminine singular subject rajanī; second clause tama ne vilaya pāyā is an ergative transitive construction where tama acts as subject of pāyā.

line-22-shakti-nahi.source: शक्ति नहीं यत्किञ्चित उसको ना सरका पाया
line-22-shakti-nahi.roman: Śakti nahīṁ yatkiñcita usako nā sarakā pāyā

words.gloss: in the least; even a little

line-22-shakti-nahi.grammarNote: Subject is elided; 'yatkiñcita' is a Sanskrit adverbial loanword ('the slightest bit'); 'sarakā pāyā' is a potential compound verb construction with negative marker 'nā'.

line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.source: तुम्ही हटा कर मुख दिखलाना जन तारो राया
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.roman: Tumhī haṭā kara mukha dikhalānā jana tāro rāyā
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.english: {0:You alone }{1,2:can remove it; }{4:show us Your }{3:face }and {6:deliver }{5:Your devotees, }{7:O King!}
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.grammarNote: 'haṭā kara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on polite imperative 'dikhalānā'; 'rāyā' is a Marathi-derived vocative honorific ('O Sovereign/Lord').

line-27-sakripa-hokar.source: सकृप होकर अपनी महिमा खुद ही सुनवाओ
line-27-sakripa-hokar.roman: Sakṛpa hokara apanī mahimā khuda hī sunavāo
line-27-sakripa-hokar.grammarNote: 'sunavāo' is a second-person plural/polite causative imperative of 'sunnā' (to hear); 'sakṛpa hokara' functions as a participial adjunct.

line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.source: देखो ऐसे देखे जैसे बालक को माता
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.roman: Dekho aise dekhe jaise bālaka ko mātā
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.grammarNote: 'dekho' is a direct imperative; 'aise... jaise' introduces a correlative comparative clause with the verb 'dekhe' agreeing with singular subject 'mātā'.

line-35-hum-hi-apni.source: हम ही अपनी खातिर तुमको कष्ट देते देवा
line-35-hum-hi-apni.roman: Hama hī apanī khātira tumako kaṣṭa dete devā
line-35-hum-hi-apni.grammarNote: 'devā' is a Marathi-influenced vocative form; 'kaṣṭa dete' has an elided auxiliary 'haiṁ' typical of verse.

line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.source: त्वद्वचनामृत प्राशन कर के देहभान खो रहा
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.roman: Tvadvacanāmṛta prāśana kara ke dehabhāna kho rahā
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.grammarNote: Tvadvacanāmṛta is a compound noun: tvad- (your) + vacana (speech) + amṛta (nectar). Prāśana kara ke is an adverbial conjunctive participial clause.

line-89-dvara-pe-baje.source: द्वार पे बाजे बजते ढोल ढमाढम गरजते
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.roman: Dvāra pe bāje bajate ḍhola ḍhamāḍhama garajate
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.english: {1:At }{0:the doorway }{2:musical instruments }{3:sound, }{4:and drums }{6:roar }{5:with a booming beat.}
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.grammarNote: Parallel imperfective participles 'bajate' and 'garajate' functioning as finite present tense verbs with omitted auxiliary 'haiṁ'. 'Ḍhamāḍhama' is an onomatopoeic adverb.

verse-2.source:
तुम संसार शक्ति लय कीना । पालन हेतु अन्न धन दीना ॥
अन्नपूर्णा हुई जग पाला । तुम ही आदि सुन्दरी बाला ॥
प्रलयकाल सब नाशन हारी । तुम गौरी शिव शंकर प्यारी ॥
शिव योगी तुम्हरे गुण गावें । ब्रह्मा विष्णु तुम्हें नित ध्यावें ॥

pralayakāla saba nāśana hārī | tuma gaurī śiva śaṅkara pyārī ||
śiva yōgī tumharē guṇa gāvēm̐ | brahmā viṣṇu tumhēṁ nita dhyāvēm̐ ||

verse-3.source:
रूप सरस्वती को तुम धारा । दे सुबुद्धि ऋषि मुनिन उबारा ॥
धर्यो रूप नरसिंह को अम्बा । परगट भई फाड़कर खम्बा ॥
रक्षा करि प्रह्लाद बचायो । हिरणाकुश को स्वर्ग पठायो ॥
लक्ष्मी रूप धरो जग माहीं । श्री नारायण अंग समाहीं ॥

dharyō rūpa narasiṅgha kō ambā | paragaṭa bhaī phāṛakara khambā ||
rakṣā kari prahlāda bacāyō | hiraṇākuśa kō svarga paṭhāyō ||
lakṣmī rūpa dharō jaga māhīm̐ | śrī nārāyaṇa aṅga samāhīm̐ ||

verse-5.source:
केहरि वाहन सोह भवानी । लांगुर वीर चलत अगवानी ॥
कर में खप्पर खड्ग विराजै । जाको देख काल डर भाजै ॥
सोहै अस्त्र और त्रिशूला । जाते उठत शत्रु हिय शूला ॥
नगरकोटि में तुम्हीं विराजत । तिहूँ लोक में डंका बाजत ॥

sōhai astra aura triśūlā | jātē uṭhata śatru hiya śūlā ||
nagarakōṭi mēṁ tumhīṁ virājata | tihūm̐ lōka mēṁ ḍaṅkā bājata ||

verse-8.source:
जोगी सुर मुनि कहत पुकारी । योग न हो बिन शक्ति तुम्हारी ॥
शंकर आचारज तप कीनो । काम अरु क्रोध जीति सब लीनो ॥
निशिदिन ध्यान धरो शंकर को । काहू काल नहिं सुमिरो तुमको ॥
शक्ति रूप को मरम न पायो । शक्ति गई तब मन पछतायो ॥

niśidina dhyāna dharō śaṅkara kō | kāhū kāla nahiṁ sumirō tumakō ||
śakti rūpa kō marama na pāyō | śakti gaī taba mana pachatāyō ||

verse-10.source:
शत्रु नाश कीजै महारानी । सुमिरौं इकचित तुम्हें भवानी ॥
करो कृपा हे मातु दयाला । ऋद्धि सिद्धि दै करहु निहाला ॥
जब लगि जिओं दया फल पाऊँ । तुम्हरो यश मैं सदा सुनाऊँ ॥
दुर्गा चालीसा जो गावै । सब सुख भोग परम पद पावै ॥
देवीदास शरण निज जानी । करहु कृपा जगदम्ब भवानी ॥

durgā cālīsā jō gāvai | saba sukha bhōga parama pada pāvai ||
dēvīdāsa śaraṇa nija jānī | karahu kṛpā jagadamba bhavānī ||

line-225.english: {3:of those who have taken refuge in}{0: Your}{2: lotus}{1: feet,}

words.gloss: of those who have taken refuge (genitive plural)

line-225.grammarNote: Genitive plural compound specifying whose distress is dispelled.

line-226.english: {0:by its own shade}{1: the torment}{2: may it dispel.}

words.gloss: the heat / torment of worldly affliction

line-226.grammarNote: Imperative 3rd singular (apa-ā-kṛ) taking accusative tāpam as direct object and instrumental svacchāyayā as means.

line-229.grammarNote: Sandhi: ramet + manaḥ -> ramēn manaḥ; manaḥ + me -> manō mē. Optative 3rd singular verb ramēt expressing prayerful wish.

line-231.english: {4:The complete destruction}{3: of sins}{2: accumulated}{1: through}{0: many}{1: births}
line-231.grammarNote: Nominative singular masculine compound functioning as the subject of bhavēd in line 232.

line-232.english: {0:would occur}{4: from the sight}{1: of Your}{3: lotus}{2: feet.}
line-232.grammarNote: Sandhi: bhavet + bhavat... Ablative of cause bhavatpādasarōjadarśanāt governing the optative bhavēd.

line-233.grammarNote: Imperative 2nd singular middle (kṣamasva) governing the accusative plural object sarvān aparādhapuñjakān.

line-243.english: {2:Done}{0: by hands}{1: and feet,}{5: born}{3: of speech}{4: and body,}{8: or}{7: born}{6: of action,}
line-243.grammarNote: Opening line of the standard kṣamāprārthanā (forgiveness prayer). The compounds are accusative singular modifiers agreeing with 'aparādham' in line 244.

line-244.english: {2:born}{0: of ears}{1: and eyes,}{3: or}{4: mental,}{5: or}{6: any offense,}

words.gloss: [any] offense (aparādham; its a merges with vā)

line-244.grammarNote: 'vāparādham' contains sandhi for 'vā' + 'aparādham'. 'aparādham' (masculine accusative singular) is the head noun for the string of qualifiers across lines 243–244.

line-175.english: {3,4:Every single day}{1: bathing}{2: and repeating sacred words}{0: in Kāśī,}
line-175.grammarNote: Elliptical nominal phrase describing Dattatreya's daily spiritual routine.

line-182.source: कमंडलु मृगछाला धारित है सिर पे
line-182.roman: kamaṇḍalu mṛgachālā dhārita hai sira pe
line-182.english: {2,3:Bearing }{0:a water-pot}{1: and a deerskin;}{4,5: on your head}
line-182.grammarNote: Passive/attributive construction with locative 'sira pe' continuing into the next line.

line-012.source: तुम्हारी उपमा तुम्हे ही शोभित है सज्जना
line-012.roman: Tumhārī upamā tumhe hī śobhit hai sajjanā
line-012.english: {2,3:Only you }{5:are }{4:a fitting }{1:comparison }{0:for yourself,}{6: O noble one.}
line-012.grammarNote: Dative experiencer construction ('tumhe... śobhit hai'). 'Sajjanā' is a vocative form addressing the Guru.

line-015.source: अजात रिपु सद्गुरु अखिल पातक भंजना
line-015.roman: Ajāt ripu sadguru akhil pātaka bhañjanā
line-015.english: {2:O true Guru}{0,1: with no enemy,}{5: destroyer}{3,4: of all sins!}
line-015.grammarNote: Vocative compounds: 'ajāt-ripu' (bahuvrīhi: having no enemy / friend to all) and 'akhil-pātaka-bhañjana' (destroyer of all sins).

line-018.source: ऐसा सुहितकारी इस जगत में कोई अन्य ना
line-018.roman: Aisā suhitakārī is jagat meṁ koī anya nā
line-018.english: {5,7:There is no}{6: other}{0,1: benefactor like you}{4: in }{2:this }{3:world.}
line-018.grammarNote: Existential sentence with negative particle 'nā' functioning as predicate and copula omitted.

line-020.source: व्यर्थ बड़बड़ करे न जाने हित स्वयं का
line-020.roman: Vyartha baṛbaṛ kare na jāne hit svayaṁ kā
line-020.english: {0,1,2:he babbles in vain}{3,4: and does not know}{5,6,7: what is good for him.}
line-020.grammarNote: Habitual 3rd-person singular verbs 'kare' and 'jāne' describing the person devoid of grace.

line-024.source: करूँ सतत सत्कृति सुमति दो जगत पावना
line-024.roman: Karūṁ satat satkṛti sumati do jagat pāvanā
line-024.english: {0,1:May I constantly do}{2: good deeds;}{3,4: grant me sound judgment,}{5,6: O purifier of the world.}
line-024.grammarNote: 'Jagat-pāvanā' is a vocative compound ('O purifier of the world'). 'Do' is a familiar/respectful imperative.

line-027.source: ऐसा श्री साईनाथ ने कहकर बताया जैसा इस बालक से
line-027.roman: Aisā Śrī Sāīnāth ne kahakar batāyā jaisā is bālak se
line-027.english: {6:Just as}{1,2,3: Śrī Sāīnātha}{4,5: spoke}{0: these words}{9: to }{7:this }{8:child,}

words.gloss: Lord Sai; Sāī (“master” or “lord”) names the revered spiritual teacher Śirḍī Sāī Bābā here

line-027.grammarNote: Ergative construction with subject 'Śrī Sāīnāth ne' and perfective transitive verb 'kahakar batāyā'.

line-041.source: साथी आखिर का साथी आखिर का साथी आखिर का किया न कोई
line-041.roman: Sāthī ākhira kā sāthī ākhira kā sāthī ākhira kā kiyā na koī
line-041.english: {0,1,2:A companion for the end,}{3,4,5: a companion for the end,}{6,7,8: a companion for the end—}{9: I found}{10,11: none.}
line-041.grammarNote: Repetition of the genitive noun phrase sāthī ākhira kā (companion of the end / lifelong refuge) before the negative predicate kiyā na koī (did not make anyone).

line-049.source: अब अंत न देखो मेरा सखा भगवंता श्रीकांता
line-049.roman: Aba anta na dekho merā sakhā bhagavantā Śrīkāntā
line-049.english: {0:Now}{2,3: do not test}{1: the limits of}{4: my endurance,}{5: O friend,}{6: O Lord,}{7: O Śrīkānta!}

words.gloss: O Śrīkānta, “beloved of Śrī (Lakṣmī)”; a name of Viṣṇu

line-049.grammarNote: Idiomatic negative imperative anta na dekho (do not test my patience/limits) followed by multiple vocatives.

line-079.source: जिसके मन में जैसा भाव उसे वैसा अनुभव
line-079.roman: Jisakē mana mē̃ jaisā bhāva usē vaisā anubhava
line-079.english: {5:To each person,}{0: according to}{3: the}{4: devotional feeling}{1,2: in their mind,}{6: a corresponding}{7: experience}
line-079.grammarNote: Correlative aphoristic syntax: jaisā bhāva (such disposition) correlates with vaisā anubhava (such experience).

line-095.source: पिला देवे माधव को रखे वचनों की लाज
line-095.roman: Pilā dēvē Mādhava kō rakhē vacanō̃ kī lāja
line-095.english: {0,1:grant a drink }{2,3:to Mādhava, }{4:and uphold }{7:the honor }{5,6:of your promises.}
line-095.grammarNote: Causative optative compound 'pilā dēvē' governing indirect object 'Mādhava kō'; 'rakhē vacanō̃ kī lāja' is an idiom for honoring one's word.

line-105.source: यवन स्वरूपी एक को दर्शन प्रगटाया
line-105.roman: yavana svarūpī eka ko darśana pragaṭāyā
line-105.english: {1:In the form of }{0:a Muslim, }{5:you revealed }{4:yourself }{3:to }{2:one person.}

words.gloss: in the form of / embodied as

line-105.grammarNote: Past transitive 'pragaṭāyā' with indirect dative object 'eka ko' and accusative object 'darśana'.

line-125.source: साष्टांग नमन वंदूं मैं चरण नैनों से देखूं रूप तेरा
line-125.roman: sāṣṭāṅga namana vandūṁ maiṁ caraṇa nainoṁ se dekhūṁ rūpa terā
line-125.english: {0,1:Prostrating my whole body,}{2,3: I bow to}{4: your feet;}{5,6: with my eyes}{7: I behold}{9: your }{8:form.}
line-125.grammarNote: Two first-person singular present verbs ('vandūṁ', 'dekhūṁ') expressing acts of physical surrender and devotion.

line-131.source: अच्युतं केशवं रामनारायणं कृष्णदामोदरं वासुदेवं हरिम्
line-131.roman: acyutaṁ keśavaṁ rāmanārāyaṇaṁ kṛṣṇadāmodaraṁ vāsudevaṁ harim

words.gloss: Keśava, the beautiful-haired one; a name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa
Rāma, a form of Viṣṇu; the name means “delightful”
Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu, the refuge of living beings who rests upon the primordial waters
Dāmodara, the one with a rope around his waist
Hari, a name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa; Hari is “the remover” of evil and suffering

line-131.grammarNote: Achyutashtakam opening; series of accusative divine epithets governed by 'bhaje' in the subsequent line.

line-132.source: श्रीधरं माधवं गोपिकावल्लभं जानकीनायकं रामचंद्रं भजे

line-132.english: {0:Śrīdhara,}{1: Mādhava,}{3: beloved}{2: of the cowherd maidens,}{5: lord}{4: of Jānakī,}{6: Rāmacandra—}{7:I adore you.}

words.gloss: Rāmacandra, “moon-like Rāma”, the hero of the Rāmāyaṇa (accusative singular); Rāma means “delightful”
I worship / adore (1st singular present middle)

line-132.grammarNote: 1st-person present verb 'bhaje' syntactically resolves the series of accusative objects spanning lines 131–132.

line-139.source: स मे कामान् कामकामाय मह्यं कामेश्वरो वैश्रवणो दधातु
line-139.roman: sa me kāmān kāmakāmāya mahyaṁ kāmeśvaro vaiśravaṇo dadhātu
line-139.english: {0:May he,}{6: Vaiśravaṇa,}{5: sovereign of desires,}{7: fulfill}{1: my }{2:wishes,}{3,4: for I long for their fulfillment.}

the sovereign of desires (kāmeśvaraḥ, nominative singular)
Vaiśravaṇa, “son of Viśravas”, Kubera, lord of wealth (nominative singular)

line-139.grammarNote: Optative-benedictory prayer with double dative recipient ('kāmakāmāya mahyaṁ') and 3rd-person imperative verb 'dadhātu'.

line-141.source: ॐ स्वस्ति साम्राज्यं भौज्यं स्वाराज्यं वैराज्यं पारमेष्ठ्यं राज्यं महाराज्यमाधिपत्यमयं समन्तपर्यायी स्यात्
line-141.roman: oṁ svasti sāmrājyaṁ bhaujyaṁ svārājyaṁ vairājyaṁ pārameṣṭhyaṁ rājyaṁ mahārājyamādhipatyamayaṁ samantaparyāyī syāt
line-141.english: {0:Oṃ,}{1: may there be well-being:}{2: universal sovereignty,}{3: bounteous dominion,}{4: self-rule,}{5: distinguished sovereignty,}{6: the highest authority,}{7: kingship,}{8: great}{9: sovereignty}{10: and paramount rule.}{14: May}{11: it}{13: extend}{12: in every direction.}

words.gloss: the highest authority; rule of the supreme station
may he be / let it be (3rd singular optative)

line-141.grammarNote: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 8.15, a royal-consecration blessing. The opening Oṃ is liturgical; the Vedic formula is governed by optative syāt and enumerates forms of sovereignty.

line-144.roman: āvikṣitasya kāmaprer viśve devāḥ sabhāsada iti

line-144.grammarNote: Completion of the Marutta verse in Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 8.15. The genitives āvikṣitasya kāmapreḥ qualify Marutta; viśve devāḥ sabhāsadaḥ is a nominal predicate.

line-151.source: बचा शेष जीवन भक्ति में ही गमावें

line-151.grammarNote: Tautological compound 'bacā śeṣa' (all the remaining); 'gamānā' in the sense of passing/spending one's days.

line-155.source: दिखे अज्ञ जन सा जन जो भी आते
line-155.roman: dikhe ajña jana sā jana jo bhī āte

line-157.source: नर देह पाया उत्तम यही है

line-157.grammarNote: Syntactic topic-comment structure: having obtained a human birth ('nara deha pāyā') is the highest blessing ('uttama yahī hai').

line-158.english: {0,1:to practice spiritual discipline}{3: is what}{2,4: gives it purpose.}

O Baba; Bābā means “father”, a respectful address to the spiritual elder Śirḍī Sāī Bābā

line-183.grammarNote: Verb 'sohata' (adorns) with compound subject 'nāgajaṭā mukuṭa' and accusative/locative 'māthā'.

line-185.source: अक्षय उनके घर में लक्ष्मी वास करे

line-192.grammarNote: Causative present participle 'darśayantam' (acc. sg. masc.) governing direct object 'mānuṣaṁ' with instrumental 'sva-bhaktecchayā'.

line-200.english: {4:By dwelling}{0: always}{3: at the base}{2: of the}{1: neem}{2: tree,}
line-200.grammarNote: Genitive singular compound sadā-nimba-vṛkṣasya depends on the ablative of place/cause mūlādhivāsāt (mūla + adhivāsa + -āt).

line-206.english: {4:Through displays}{0: of countless}{1: unheard-of}{2: and inconceivable}{3: divine games,}
line-206.grammarNote: Instrumental plural compound (aneka + aśruta + atarkya + līlā-vilāsaiḥ) expressing the means of manifestation.

line-209.english: {0:for the righteous,}{2: a delightful}{1: garden of rest,}
line-209.grammarNote: Sandhi: eva + abhirāmam. Accusative singular describing the Lord as the peaceful grove for the virtuous.

line-226.grammarNote: Imperative 3rd singular (apa-ā-kṛ) taking accusative tāpam as direct object and instrumental svacchāyayā as means.

line-232.grammarNote: Sandhi: bhavet + bhavat... Ablative of cause bhavatpādasarōjadarśanāt governing the optative bhavēd.

line-233.grammarNote: Imperative 2nd singular middle (kṣamasva) governing the accusative plural object sarvān aparādhapuñjakān.

line-243.english: {2:Committed}{0: with hands}{1: or feet,}{5: arising}{3: from speech}{4: or the body,}{8: or}{7: from}{6: actions,}
line-243.grammarNote: Opening line of the standard kṣamāprārthanā (forgiveness prayer). The compounds are accusative singular modifiers agreeing with 'aparādham' in line 244.

line-244.english: {6:offenses}{2: arising}{0: from hearing}{1: or sight,}{3,5: or}{4: from the mind—}

Source passage retains this feature after the English repairs: Darkness is born again, but by the Guru's grace, ignorance is not. / By your grace, all distresses pass away. / O Lord Śrī Sāī, ocean of grace, who grants the fulfilment of every aim to all people!

Source passage retains this feature after the English repairs: One may be very clever, but if there is no grace of the Guru, / he babbles in vain and does not know what is good for him. / O Infinite One, how can we come to you for refuge?

Source passage retains this feature after the English repairs: By your words, the bonds of worldly existence are severed in a moment. / freed from the flood of evils born of worldly existence, they / fully attain the supreme abode of liberation.

Source passage retains this feature after the English repairs: Without you there is no refuge on this earthly plane. / I am drowning in the ocean of worldly existence; rescue me! / I have come for refuge, with true devotion and folded hands, O Lord. / I have no refuge but the lotus feet of the glorious supreme Lord Sāī.

Source passage retains this feature after the English repairs: By body, by speech, by mind or by senses, by intellect or by self, or from innate disposition— / whatever I perform, all of that I surrender to the Supreme Narayana.

featureDispositions.reason: The final verse promises that Sai the Guru will grant blessings and dispel Kali’s play.
The contrasting corruption and false search for peace culminate in asking who but Sai will show the path.
The repeated questions who will sustain and protect us are answered explicitly Sai Baba.
Placing our heads at Sai’s feet is a concrete presentation of self in worship, beyond a generic praise epithet.
The singer exhorts everyone to go to Shirdi, an explicit devotional journey.
The Guru is the one who conveys devotees, and Sai is directly called the supreme Guru.
Sai Baba answers the refrain, shows the path, receives the bowed heads and gives blessings.
