one should go; we shall leave

line-073.grammarNote: jāve and nijave are impersonal potential/optative verb forms used as polite imperatives. pāvalā agrees with masculine prasāda.

line-008.grammarNote: Kheḷoniyā is the absolutive/conjunctive participle ('having played'); vistāra kelā is an ergative compound verb.

line-041.source: झाले असतील कष्ट अतिशय तुमचे या देहाला हो
line-041.roman: Jhālē astatīla kaṣṭa atiśaya tumacē yā dēhālā hō
line-041.grammarNote: Jhālē astatīla forms a compound presumptive past ('must have occurred'). dēhālā is dative/accusative marked with -lā.

line-046.source: सोडुनि जाया दुःख वाटते बाबांच्या चरणांशी हो

line-046.grammarNote: Impersonal dative/experiencer syntax: sōḍuni jāyā duḥkha vāṭatē ('leaving to go feels sorrowful'). Bābāñcyā carries honorific plural genitive -ñcyā.

line-047.source: सोडुनि जाया दुःख वाटते साईंच्या चरणांशी हो

line-056.grammarNote: śiḍakāvā didhalā is a conjunct verb ('gave a sprinkling'). supremācā = su- + prēma + genitive -cā.

line-057.source: पायघड्या घातल्या सुंदर नवविधा भक्ती बाबा नवविधा भक्ती

line-057.grammarNote: pāyaghaḍyā is feminine plural (from pāyaghaḍī); ghātalyā is the agreeing feminine plural perfect participle.

line-1.source: मैं मेरा घर जाळिया रे जोगिया जियो, दीया पलीता हाथ
line-1.roman: maiṁ mērā ghara jāḷiyā rē jōgiyā jiyō, dīyā palītā hātha
line-1.grammarNote: First-person Rajasthani transitive past construction with subject maiṁ, direct object mērā ghara, and verb phrase jāḷiyā ... dīyā palītā hātha. The vocative address rē jōgiyā jiyō is parenthetical.

line-2.source: कोई जाळो घर आपणो रे जोगिया जियो, चलो हमारे साथ
line-2.roman: kōī jāḷō ghara āpaṇō rē jōgiyā jiyō, calō hamārē sātha
line-2.grammarNote: An open invitation addressed to an unspecified listener: burn your own house and walk with us. The two verbs jāḷō and calō address that listener.

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful Lord invoked here as the supreme divine reality; the name is also that of Rāma of Ayodhyā
juice; here, the sweetness of devotion pictured as a drink

refrain-1.grammarNote: Nominal phrase headed by the compound rāma rasa preceded by the exclamatory/emphatic particle kai.

refrain-2.source: मीठो घणो रे जोगिया जियो, पीये अमर होय जाय
refrain-2.roman: mīṭhō ghaṇō rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīyē amara hōya jāya
refrain-2.grammarNote: Adjectival clause mīṭhō ghaṇō describing rāma rasa, followed by the participial conditional clause pīyē and compound verb hōya jāya with complement amara.

line-3.source: घर जाळ्यो घर ऊभरे रे जोगिया जियो, घर राखो घर जाय
line-3.roman: ghara jāḷyō ghara ūbharē rē jōgiyā jiyō, ghara rākhō ghara jāya
line-3.english: {0:If the house }{1:is burned, }{2:the home }{3:is saved, }{4:O }{6:noble }{5:ascetic; }{7:if the house }{8:is kept, }{9:the home }{10:is lost.}
line-3.grammarNote: Balanced antithetical couplet with polysemous ghara (first outer house, then inner true home). Each half consists of an absolute conditional participle (jāḷyō / rākhō) and an intransitive present verb (ūbharē / jāya).

line-4.source: एक अचम्भो मैं देखियो रे जोगिया जियो, मढ़ो काल ने खाय
line-4.roman: ēka acambhō maiṁ dēkhiyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, maḍhō kāla nē khāya
line-4.grammarNote: Transitive main clause ēka acambhō maiṁ dēkhiyō followed by the subordinate content clause maḍhō kāla nē khāya with maḍhō as subject and kāla marked with the postposition nē.

line-5.source: आगे आगे धाव जळे रे जोगिया जियो, पीछे हरिया होय
line-5.roman: āgē āgē dhāva jaḷē rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīchē hariyā hōya
line-5.grammarNote: Reduplicated spatial adverb āgē āgē with subject dhāva and intransitive verb jaḷē, contrasted with the adverbial phrase pīchē hariyā hōya.

line-6.source: बलिहारी उन रूखड़ी रे जोगिया जियो, जड़ काटो फल होय
line-6.roman: balihārī una rūkhaṛī rē jōgiyā jiyō, jaṛa kāṭō phala hōya
line-6.english: {0:I offer myself }{1:to that }{2:little tree, }{3:O }{5:noble }{4:ascetic: }{6,7:cut its root, }{9:and it bears }{8:fruit.}

words.gloss: I offer myself in devotion; an expression of self-surrender

line-6.grammarNote: Devotional noun balihārī governing oblique demonstrative and diminutive noun una rūkhaṛī, followed by absolute participial clause jaṛa kāṭō and result phala hōya.

line-7.source: ध्रुव पियो प्रह्लाद पियो रे जोगिया जियो, पीये रह्यो रविदास
line-7.roman: dhruva piyō prahlāda piyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīyē rahyō ravidāsa
line-7.grammarNote: Compound declarative line with simple past clauses dhruva piyō and prahlāda piyō, combined with the continuous aspectual construction pīyē rahyō ravidāsa.

line-8.source: भगत कबीर रस पीये रह्यो रे जोगिया जियो, फेर पीवण री आस
line-8.roman: bhagata kabīra rasa pīyē rahyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, phēra pīvaṇa rī āsa

words.gloss: juice; here, the sweetness of devotion pictured as a drink

line-8.grammarNote: Subject bhagata kabīra with continuous verb pīyē rahyō taking direct object rasa, followed by the Rajasthani genitive nominal phrase phēra pīvaṇa rī āsa.

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful Lord invoked here as the supreme divine reality; the name is also that of Rāma of Ayodhyā
